channel.title: iHeartTheatre Reviews
channel.description: Theatre reviews from Melbourne and Victoria — musicals, plays, comedy, circus and more. Reviewed by Deanna Amato and Penelope Quinn.

item.title: The Good Life
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: There's something instantly comforting about The Good Life; what was a quintessentially English sitcom from the mid-1970s, has somehow managed to age without losing its warmth.

item.title: Dying: A Memoir
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Genevieve Morris breaks the ice as she enters through the audience, setting the tone perfectly, cheeky, warm and unafraid comedic timing, disarming us with a vulnerability that feels bracingly real.

item.title: The Lucky Country
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: The Lucky Country ushers in a bold new chapter of Australian storytelling. Written, composed, and performed by Vidya Makan and co-created and directed by Sashi Nair.

item.title: Greeking Out
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Greeking Out, created and performed by Rebecca Perich feels a little like first day of class, if your teacher was equal parts mythologist, stand-up comic and your best friend.

item.title: Mamma Mia!
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Stepping into the Playhouse, the atmosphere was already set, mist drifting, the low rumble of waves complete with birds chirping and the glow of an ambient sunset.

item.title: Into The Woods Jr.
item.dc:creator: Penelope Quinn
item.description: As soon as we stepped into the venue, we noticed pine trees in the foyer and around the stage made everything feel like we were already in the woods before the show even started.

item.title: Mother Play
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: A clever and moving portrait of a family unravelling, Mother Play holds up a mirror to intergenerational trauma, queer identity and the lifelong push-pull between devotion and destruction.

item.title: Asexual Fantasies and Hopeless Aromantics
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Sophie Harvey's Asexual Fantasies and Hopeless Aromantics is not your typical cabaret. It gently and powerfully invites you into the deeply personal, quietly revolutionary experience of asexuality.

item.title: Mary Poppins
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: From the very first moment, MDMS's Mary Poppins at Karralyka Theatre, swept us up and transported us to Cherry Tree Lane, where a full-scale, life-sized dollhouse set the scene.

item.title: BATSH*T
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: I was looking forward to seeing Batsh*t at The Arts Centre for its warm ambience, luxe carpet and comfy seats that invite an exhale before the house lights dim.

item.title: Girl on the Train
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Entering the theatre, you'll be greeted with a warm sense of nostalgia as you pass the Hall of Fame where cast photos from productions past, line the walls.

item.title: Josephine Wants To Dance
item.dc:creator: Penelope Quinn
item.description: When the lights went down, I held my breath because I just knew Josephine Wants To Dance was going to be something special and it really was!

item.title: Circus Oz – Non Stop
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Circus Oz's latest spectacle at the Melbourne International Comedy Festival is a full body, technicolour collision and a glorious rebellion against the mundane.

item.title: Bubble Laboratory – Bubble Show in Space
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: If you think you've seen every kind of bubble trick under the sun, Bubble Laboratory in Space at the Melbourne International Comedy Festival will prove you delightfully wrong.

item.title: Tristan McLindon – DM for Deception
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: From the moment we arrived at this show, we find pens and pieces of paper placed on every few seats, from this point DM for Deception begins its slippery slide into illusion.

item.title: Lou Wall – Breaking the 5th Wall
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: In Lies I Told My Therapist, the line between truth and fiction isn't just blurred, it's deleted. Even the sequel doubles down on chaos and charm.

item.title: The Little Mermaid Junior
item.dc:creator: Penelope Quinn
item.description: From the moment we walked in, there were so many cute under the sea themed things, even the toilets were signed for mermaids and mermen! Everyone was so friendly.

item.title: Abracadickhead
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Liam Jumpertz's Abracadickhead is a comedic spectacle that intertwines magic and humor, leaving audiences both bewildered and amused.

item.title: Ruby Wax – I'm Not As Well As I Thought I Was
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Ruby Wax is a comedic force of nature and in I'm Not As Well As I Thought I Was, she delivers a performance that is as raw as it is exuberantly funny.

item.title: Romeo & Juliet
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: In a modern yet nostalgic reimagining of Shakespeare's timeless tragedy, the Melbourne Shakespeare Company delivers a compelling production of Romeo and Juliet.

item.title: Robin Hood
item.dc:creator: Penelope Quinn
item.description: Robin Hood, a new family musical by Melbourne Shakespeare Company, took my whole family on a very amusing adventure into the enchanted forest of Sherwood.

item.title: TRUTH
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Truth storms into Melbourne's iconic Malthouse Theatre with an uncompromising exploration of power, secrecy and the human collateral of exposing truth.

item.title: The Wind in the Willows
item.dc:creator: Penelope Quinn
item.description: The Wind in the Willows by the Australian Shakespeare Company was an absolute dream, to watch theatre in the gardens with a picnic!

item.title: MUSE
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: The NICA end of year showcase: MUSE was an inspiring exploration, blending raw physicality with intimate vulnerability.

item.title: A Christmas Carol
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: The opening night of A Christmas Carol at Melbourne's Comedy Theatre delivered a visually and emotionally charged experience, delightfully blending theatrical spectacle with timeless storytelling.

item.title: Shakespeare-In-Between: Romeo & Juliet
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Shakespeare In Between: Romeo and Juliet is a remarkable spectacle reimagining the timeless tale, weaving the untold stories of Verona's residents into the narrative.

item.title: YOUR NAME MEANS DREAM
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Your Name Means Dream at Red Stitch Theatre is a captivating exploration of relationships between humans and machines, brought to life with remarkable depth.

item.title: My Brilliant Apocalypse: The Return of Barry Brilliant
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: My Brilliant Apocalypse: The Return of Barry Brilliant at the Melbourne Fringe Festival is an artistically critical, thought-provoking experience.

item.title: Secret Girl Stuff
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Secret Girl Stuff is a powerful and evocative production that delivers a rude awakening to the realities of being a woman in a so-called first world country.

item.title: Apocrypha by Oozing Future
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: Apocrypha was a captivating blend of futuristic and primal mediums, offering a unique and thought-provoking experience.

item.title: Seussical The Musical
item.dc:creator: Deanna Amato
item.description: OPAC's recent production of Seussical was nothing short of magical. This vibrant and heartwarming musical brought the world of Dr. Seuss to life.

item.title: Imagine LIVE
item.dc:creator: Penelope Quinn
item.description: First of all, there were so many punny jokes that made everyone laugh. The show was delightfully charming and I loved how interactive it was.

item.title: Into The Woods Jnr
item.dc:creator: Penelope Quinn
item.description: Watching Into the Woods Jnr by Eltham Little Theatre Inc, directed by Gareth Clarke, was like a fairy tale party!
